chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him narrated to us, he said: My grandfather narrated to me, he said: Dawud ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn Zayd narrated to us, he said: I heard a group of the members of my household saying

When Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) returned from the land of Abyssinia, where he had been migrating, and that was the day of the conquest of Khaybar, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood up for him, kissed him between the eyes, and then said: 'I do not know which of the two I am more pleased with: the return of Ja'far, or the conquest of Khaybar.' And I have narrated the traditions that I reported in this meaning in the book 'Virtues of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)'.

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْحَبَشَةِ: The land of Abyssinia (modern-day Ethiopia), where early Muslims migrated to escape persecution
key_terms.بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ: Between the eyes, referring to the forehead area
key_terms.جَعْفَرَ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, a prominent companion of the Prophet known as Dh al-Ri'ah (Possessor of the Wing)
key_terms.فَتْحِ خَيْبَرَ: The conquest of Khaybar, a significant military event in Islamic history
key_terms.فَضَائِلِ جَعْفَرَ: Virtues/merits of Ja'far, referring to a specific book or section detailing his merits

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say when Ja'far ibn Abi Talib returned from Abyssinia?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this event in *Al-Khisal*, noting that Ja'far's return from Abyssinia coincided with the conquest of Khaybar, a timing that underscores the dual triumph of diplomatic resilience and military victory. The Prophet’s declaration of equal joy highlights Ja'far’s unique status as 'Dhul-Qarnayn' and the spiritual weight of the Banu Hashim's safe return, which was viewed as a divine blessing comparable to the opening of a major fortress.
